title: A Round of Golf
description: Visit a golf course through familiar equipment, features, and scoring words.
cardDescription: Visit a golf course through familiar equipment, features, and scoring words.
focus: The clues use ordinary golf vocabulary without requiring tournament records. Positions and purposes distinguish the terms.
solvingTip: Look for a playing object, a part of the course, or a score description.
words: Game played by hitting a small ball toward a series of holes
Implement swung to strike a golf ball
Small support holding a ball before an opening shot
Closely cut area surrounding a golf hole
Main closely cut route between tee and green
Longer grass bordering a golf fairway
Short golf stroke usually played on the green
Long opening golf stroke from a teeing area
Expected number of strokes assigned to a hole
Score one stroke below par on a hole
Score one stroke above par on a hole
Person who carries clubs and assists a golfer
Marker showing a hole’s position on the green

answerNotes.PAR: Par is the assigned expected stroke count. Birdie and bogey describe scores relative to it.
answerNotes.BIRDIE: A birdie is one under par. The word identifies a score rather than a small bird.
answerNotes.BOGEY: A bogey is one over par. Its position above par distinguishes it from a birdie.
answerNotes.ROUGH: Rough is the longer grass beside the fairway. It is a course area rather than a general comment on a difficult day.

title: An Afternoon at the Bowling Alley
description: Set up familiar bowling words for lanes, pins, equipment, and results.
cardDescription: Set up familiar bowling words for lanes, pins, equipment, and results.
focus: The clues describe tenpin bowling. Some answers name objects, while others name a unit of play or the result of a roll.
solvingTip: Check whether a clue asks for equipment, a score result, or a place on the lane.
words: Game of rolling a ball toward standing pins
Long surface along which a bowling ball rolls
One standing target in tenpin bowling
Heavy finger-holed object rolled in bowling
Channel along either side of a bowling lane
All ten pins knocked down with the first roll of a frame
All ten pins knocked down using both rolls of a frame
One of ten scoring divisions in a standard tenpin game
Separated standing pins left after a first roll
Violation associated with stepping beyond the bowling line
Special footwear worn on the bowling approach
To send a bowling ball along the lane
Recorded points earned during a bowling game

answerNotes.STRIKE: A strike clears ten pins on the first roll of a frame. A spare uses two rolls.
answerNotes.FRAME: A frame is one scoring division. The term does not mean the border around a picture here.
answerNotes.SPLIT: A split leaves separated pins standing. The gap between them makes the arrangement distinctive.
answerNotes.GUTTER: A gutter is a channel beside the lane. The clue names a bowling feature rather than roof drainage.

title: Bocce in the Park
description: Discover bocce through familiar ball-game words and simple descriptions of the playing area.
cardDescription: Discover bocce through familiar ball-game words and simple descriptions of the playing area.
focus: The clues identify objects, positions, and actions used around bocce. Direct definitions introduce the small target ball and related terms.
solvingTip: Look for a ball, a surface, a position, or an action; several answers are ordinary short words.
words: Lawn or court game played by rolling balls near a small target
Small target ball used in bocce
Rounded playing object rolled toward a bocce target
Prepared playing area for a bocce match
To move a bocce ball along the ground
To throw a ball with a gentle upward motion
Object toward which the playing balls are directed
One unit credited when scoring a bocce round
Players acting together on one side
One completed stage of a bocce game
Close in distance to the target ball
At a greater distance from the target
Fine granular material used on some playing surfaces
To compare the distances between balls and a target

answerNotes.PALLINO: Pallino names the small target ball in bocce. The larger playing balls are directed toward it.
answerNotes.COURT: Court names the playing area here. It is not a place where legal cases are heard.
answerNotes.ROUND: Round is a stage of play in this clue. The same word also describes the shape of the balls.
answerNotes.MEASURE: Measure is a verb for comparing distances here. The clue asks for an action rather than one particular measuring tool.

title: Croquet on the Lawn
description: Step onto a croquet lawn through familiar equipment, shapes, and movement words.
cardDescription: Step onto a croquet lawn through familiar equipment, shapes, and movement words.
focus: The clues describe the game’s objects through direct definitions. A few terms identify the hoops and upright markers used on the lawn.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue names something struck, something swung, or something passed through.
words: Lawn game played by striking balls through hoops
Long-handled striking tool used in croquet
Rounded object struck through croquet hoops
Hoop through which a croquet ball is played
Arched opening used as a target in croquet
Upright post used as a croquet marker
Area of closely cut grass used for a garden game
Part of a croquet mallet gripped by the player
One striking action with the mallet
One player’s opportunity to play croquet
Opening suggested by the shape of a croquet hoop
Short upright marker driven into the ground
Arranged route followed through the croquet targets

answerNotes.MALLET: A croquet mallet has a long handle and a striking head. The clue names the complete implement.
answerNotes.WICKET: Wicket names a croquet hoop here. The word also has a different sporting use in cricket.
answerNotes.STROKE: A stroke is one strike with the mallet. It names the action rather than the mallet head.
answerNotes.COURSE: Course is the arranged playing route here. It does not refer to a serving within a meal.

title: Tennis at the Local Courts
description: Explore tennis through familiar equipment, court features, and short scoring words.
cardDescription: Explore tennis through familiar equipment, court features, and short scoring words.
focus: These clues define tennis vocabulary. Knowing the purpose or position of an object can help as much as following the sport.
solvingTip: Look for a piece of equipment, a playing action, or a score term.
words: Racket game played by hitting a ball across a net
Stringed implement swung to hit a tennis ball
Mesh barrier stretched across a tennis court
Marked playing surface for a tennis match
Stroke used to put the ball into play in tennis
Return struck before the ball bounces
Serve the receiver does not touch
Tennis score in which both sides have at least three points and are level
Tennis word for a score of zero
Group of tennis games forming part of a match
Boundary marking on a tennis court
Tennis format with two players on each side

answerNotes.LOVE: Love means zero in tennis scoring. The sporting context differs from affection in everyday use.
answerNotes.DEUCE: Deuce is the level score reached at forty-all and after later equal points. A player must then gain the required advantage.
answerNotes.VOLLEY: A volley is hit before a bounce. It differs from a groundstroke played after the ball reaches the court.
answerNotes.ACE: An ace is an untouched legal serve. The word has a separate meaning as a playing card.
